name: Sikasil-702
paste:
SIKASIL®-702: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikasil®-702, September 2025, Version 01.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/f/sikasil-702.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikasil®-702 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2025, Version 01.04).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sikasil®-702 is a premium grade one-component neutral curing silicone sealant with good adhesion, elasticity and weatherability for all trade and home internal and external sealing applications.
    - Sikasil®-702 is easy to apply does not contain any fillers and cures through the absorption of atmospheric moisture to form a tough flexible waterproof seal.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikasil®-702 All Purpose is suitable for:
    - Kitchens & Bathrooms
    - Basins
    - Baths
    - Toilets
    - Shower screens & tiled wet areas
    - Benchtops & Around splashbacks
    - Roofs & Gutters including polycarbonate
    - Around plumbing fixtures and penetrations
    - Sealing windows & door frames
    - General interior & exterior sealing
    - Not suitable for natural stone, some porous materials and copper
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikasil®-702
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: PREMIUM NEUTRAL CURE MULTI-PURPOSE PURE SILICONE SEALANT
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Green Building Council of Australia Green Star Design & As Built V1.3-13.1.1B
    - Green Building Council of Australia Green Star Interiors V1.3-12.1.1B
2.3 Certificates and test reports.
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018 - Water Potable Approved
    - Green Building Council Of Australia, Low VOC V1.3- 13.1.1B & V1.3-12.1.1B
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018: cited with a stated property or value; listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1); Technical Information > Contact with water (p.2).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - ISO 8339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Secant tensile modulus (p.2).
    - ISO 7389: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Elastic recovery (p.2).
    - ASTM C719: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - CQP 049-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Curing rate (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - No fillers
    - Neutral cure
    - Non-corrosive
    - Interior & exterior use
    - Mould resistant
    - Good adhesion to most common building materials including: glass, ceramic, painted surfaces, concrete, wood, polycarbonate, most metal & most plastic
    - High movement capability ± 25%
    - Very easy to apply & fast curing
    - Excellent temperature resistance (-40°C to +150°C)
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Neutral cure silicone
    - Colour: White, Off White, Alabaster, Almond Ivory, Taupe, Beige, Tile Grey, Mid Grey, Grey, Earth Grey, Bluestone, Pewter, Charcoal, Black & Translucent
    - Density: ~1.01 kg/l
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Green building: 49 grams per litre as VOC content
    - Shore A hardness: ~28 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Secant tensile modulus: At +23°C and 100% elongation 0.45 N/mm²; At -20°C and 100% elongation 0.60 N/mm² (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~250% (ISO 37)
    - Elastic recovery: ~90% (ISO 7389)
    - Movement capability: ± 25% (ASTM C719)
    - Contact with water: AS/NZS 4020:2018 - Water Potable Approved
2.8 Service temperature.
    | Maximum | +150°C |
    | Minimum | -40°C |
2.9 Joint design. For movement joints, the width must be at least 6 mm and should not exceed 45 mm. For non-movement joints such as connection joints in interior areas, the joint width can be less than 6 mm. The joint dimensions must be designed to suit the movement capability of the sealant. In all cases joints must be at least 6 mm deep, or a have a width to depth ratio of 1 : 0.5 (for exceptions, see table below).
    | Joint Width (mm) | Joint Depth (mm) | Joint Length /300 ml ctg |
    | 6 | 4 | 12 m |
    | 9 | 5 | 6 m |
    | 12 | 6 | 4 m |
    For more information about joint design and calculations refer to the Sika document Design guideline: Dimensioning of construction joints or contact Sika Technical Services.
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 300ml cartridge
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
2.11 Storage conditions. The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +25°C. Always refer to packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2025, Version 01.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry, sound and free from oils, grease, dust, cement laitance and loose or friable particles. For optimum adhesion, joint durability and critical, high performance applications the following priming and/or pre-treatment procedures must be followed, primers and activators are adhesion promoters and not an alternative to improve poor preparation/cleaning of the joint surface. The substrate should be of sufficient strength to withstand the stress induced by the sealant during movement. Use techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, grit blasting or other suitable mechanical methods to remove all weak substrate material. Repair all damaged joint edges with suitable Sika® repair products.
    - IMPORTANT: Avoid excessive application of primer causing puddles. Refer to Product Data Sheets for necessary flash off times.
3.3 Non-porous substrates. Aluminium, anodised aluminium, stainless steel, galvanised steel and glazed tiles
    - Lightly roughen the surface with a fine abrasive pad.
    - Clean the surface.
    - Pretreat the surface using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth.
    - Lightly roughen the surface with a fine abrasive pad.
    - Clean the surface. Pretreat the surface using Sika® Aktivator-205 with a clean cloth.
    - Allow a waiting time.
    - Apply Sika® Primer-3 N by brush.
    Other metals, such as brass, bronze, and titanium-zinc
3.4 Non-porous substrates - Float glass, coated glass and Powder-coated metals.
    - Clean the surface.
    - Pretreat the surface using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth.
3.5 Non-porous substrates - Pvc.
    - Clean the surface.
    - Pretreat the surface using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth.
3.6 Porous substrates. Concrete, aerated concrete and cement based renders, mortars and bricks.
    - Prime surface using Sika® Primer-3 N applied by brush.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2025, Version 01.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Backing material: Use closed cell polyethylene foam backing rod or backing tape
    - Sagging: Non Sag
4.3 Curing rate.
    | ~4.0mm / 24 hours | At 23°C / 50 % R.H. |
    Test method printed: (CQP 049-2)
4.4 Skinning time.
    | ~10 minutes | At 23°C / 50% R.H. |
    Test method printed: (CQP 019-1)
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - Masking
    - It is recommended to use masking tape where neat or exact joint lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time after finishing.
4.6 Application method / tools - Joint Backing.
    - After the required substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth.
    - Priming
    - If required, prime the joint surfaces as recommended in substrate preparation.
    - Application
    - Sikasil®-702 is supplied ready to use. Prepare the end of the cartridge / foil pack before or after inserting into the sealant gun then fit the nozzle. Extrude Sikasil®- 702 into the joint ensuring that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoiding any air entrapment.
    - Finishing
    - As soon as possible after application, sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion and a smooth finish. Use a compatible tooling agent (e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) to smooth the joint surface. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Remover-208 immediately after use. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin use Sika® Cleaner-350H.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sikasil®-702 cannot be overpainted.
    - When applying sealant into a previously silicone sealed joint, ensure all residue is removed from joint.
    - Do not use on natural stone.
    - Do not use on bituminous substrates, natural rubber or any building materials which might leach oils, plasticisers or solvents that could degrade the sealant.
    - EPDM or other gaskets in direct contact must be tested for compatibility prior to application.
    - Do not use on pre-stressed polyacrylate and polycarbonate as it may cause environmental stress cracking (crazing).
    - Do not use on copper.
    - Do not use Sikasil®-702 in areas which are exposed to strong oxidising acids (e.g. nitric acid) and bases.
    - Do not use to seal joints in or around swimming pools for joints under water pressure or permanent water immersion.
    - Do not use Sikasil®-702 in totally confined spaces as it requires atmospheric moisture to cure.
    - Do not use for medical or pharmaceutical applications.
    - Colour variations may occur due to the exposure in service to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV radiation (especially with white colour shade). This effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature.
    | Maximum | +40°C |
    | Minimum | +5°C |
5.3 Substrate temperature.
    | Maximum | +40°C |
    | Minimum | +5°C |
    Note: The substrate temperature must be +3°C above dew point temperature and free from frost and ice.
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Do not use Sikasil®-702 in totally confined spaces as it requires atmospheric moisture to cure.
    - Colour variations may occur due to the exposure in service to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV radiation (especially with white colour shade). This effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Shore A hardness: ~28 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Secant tensile modulus: At +23°C and 100% elongation 0.45 N/mm²; At -20°C and 100% elongation 0.60 N/mm² (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~250% (ISO 37)
    - Elastic recovery: ~90% (ISO 7389)
    - Movement capability: ± 25% (ASTM C719)
    - Curing rate: ~4.0mm / 24 hours | At 23°C / 50 % R.H. (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~10 minutes | At 23°C / 50% R.H. (CQP 019-1)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikasil®-702, September 2025, Version 01.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/f/sikasil-702.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikasil®-702, version 16/10/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/0/sds-sikasil-702.pdf
    - Brochure: Sikasil-702 All Purpose, version 11/05/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/z/Leaflet%20Sikasil-702.pdf
    - Colour chart: Sikasil 702 Silicone Colour Card, version 13/02/2023, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/Sikasil%20702%20Silicone%20blob%20card%202021%20PANTONE%20BLOB%20COLOURS%20DIGITAL%20FIN%20R1.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
